utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number, IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the Prosecution. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Good afternoon, Your Honours. May I proceed with my examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness, following -- at the end of your testimony at the last occasion you were here, we started to -- I started asking you some questions regarding your wife during the period of time following the events of the 16th and 17th of April, and I think you said that she left Bosanski Samac on the 16th of April. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Throughout the period of time that you were incarcerated and up until your release, did she remain out of Bosanski Samac in Croatian-held territory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: She had your children with her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was she able to travel for at least a period of that time, that is, the time between your arrest and your eventual exchange, into Odzak from time to time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Following your release - sorry, your exchange - did you presumably talk to her about the circumstances of your incarceration and attempts -- your attempts or just the issue of exchanges generally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did she discuss any attempts or any interest that she had shown in getting you exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you recall -- or rather, did she report to you of anything that she had heard regarding you and/or the possibility of you being exchanged during the period of time that you were held in custody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you now tell the Chamber what it was that she reported to you regarding that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes. Please go ahead and tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: After my exchange, I talked to my wife on several occasions about why they were unable to exchange me earlier, and she told me that she went through Slavonia and Slavonski Svilaj on the ferry to Odzak to seek that I be exchanged. She had great confidence in herself, and she wanted to meet the people who were involved in exchanges. On one occasion she told me that she was present when the conversation took place between -- the conversation, she overheard it over the radio transmitter, and the conversation was between somebody in Odzak and somebody in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did she report to you who -- as to who were the personalities speaking on the radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: She said that she had heard the voice of Simo Zaric and the voice of Milos Bogdanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did she report to you what Simo Zaric had said, apparently over the radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: As they were discussing the exchanges, she told me that there were some two or three options and none of it was acceptable. And then she heard the voice of Simo. She heard that he asked that two JNA pilots be exchanged for me. Then the conversation was disrupted, and then the exchange was not discussed any more. She did not remember who had said that I was in Serbia at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. What I want to be clear about is this -- I withdraw that question. Did she often -- did she report to you that she often went to listen to the exchange negotiations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, she was able to overhear that particular conversation because she did not believe that people from the Croatian side had sought me, and because of that she was brought into that room and told, "Well, here. Come on in, and you will be able to hear the negotiations yourself."

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, as at this point of time, in 1992, how long had your wife known Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, she has known him as long as I have. I knew him a bit better because I socialised with him more. However, she knew him quite well too, because he was the one who hired her when he was the secretary.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What do you mean "hired her when he was the secretary"? What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the time when he was appointed secretary of the secretariat, or rather, the head of the secretariat, and after that he hired her. My wife worked at the same place where I did, and she knew him quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And she presumably, therefore, would have had an opportunity to speak to him and hear him speak and hear his voice.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's quite natural for her to recognise his voice upon hearing it, because she had known him for 20 years, worked in the same organisation and listened to his voice for that many years, so it was not difficult for her to recognise his voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. One last question: You have already described your exchange in detail. I don't propose to go into the details of that any more, but just one last question. As at April of 1992, and before the events of the night of the 16th and 17th of April, had you had any plans or intentions to uproot yourself from your home and leave Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Witness. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Zaric's Defence, I will cross-examine the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry. Your Honours, may I just seek the assistance of the usher to remove the ELMO machine over a bit? I can't see the witness at all, and I'd just like to be able to see him when he's testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. I will address you as "Witness A" during this cross-examination. Please do not consider this a sign of my disrespect. It is just that we need to keep your identity secret, so this is the main reason why I will be addressing you in this manner. My name is Aleksandar Lazarevic. I am an attorney representing Mr. Simo Zaric in this trial. And on behalf of my client I will be putting some questions to you. The questions are designed in such a way as to elicit a yes-or-no answer from you. If you do not remember something, then please just tell us so. If you do not understand something, then please again tell me that you did not understand the question quite well, and then I will either reformulate it or try to clear it in another way. Since you and I can understand each other well -- but for the sake of the interpreters, the Prosecution, and the Trial Chamber, I will ask you to make a short pause after my question before giving your answer so that we do not overlap and so that we make it easier for the interpreters. I will also have to switch off my mike before letting you answer the question so that your voice is not overheard through my microphone. And before I start putting questions to you, I would like to tell you, on behalf of my client, that he sincerely regrets everything that you and your family have suffered during these unfortunate events in Bosnia and Herzegovina. My client has asked me to convey this to you. And now let's start with questions. But before we do that, let me just tell you this: In view of your past health problems, if you should feel any discomfort, please tell us immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, for easy handling of this cross-examination, I believe that the witness should have his statement, given according to Rule 92 bis. The number of this statement is P132.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And I believe he should have it in front of himself, because I will refer to some paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can the witness be given the statement, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You have your statement in front of you. I will refer to certain paragraphs of your statement during my cross-examination, and I might ask for clarification or I might ask you to elaborate on some things that I consider important, so I think it will be the easiest if you have that statement in front of you. Now I will ask you to turn to page 2, paragraph 6 of your statement. In this paragraph, you spoke about certain tasks that you performed while you worked for the Secretariat of the Interior, and in your last statement you mentioned some certain security tasks that you personally were involved in. I would like to ask you now whether you can confirm that Mr. Zaric, who at the time was chief of police, was in charge of that very operation of securing the railway at the time when President Tito's train passed through that region. Was Mr. Zaric the superior person at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was my superior at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, such things as securing the area for the travel of the president, was that something that the department of the state security was in charge of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this paragraph, I describe things that I had performed, together with my colleagues, during my career, and I simply made an example, gave an example, saying that at that time the then president of Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Josip Broz Tito, had passed through the region. Since we were at the very entrance into Bosnia and Herzegovina, we were there where the railway passed, the railway which he travelled, and I, as a member of police at the time, was involved in securing this area where he passed through.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. But in any case, Mr. Zaric was in charge of such tasks at the time, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was in charge in our organisation at that level, and I suppose that somebody else was in charge of the entire project of securing this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's all I wanted to hear. Now, sir, in this statement that you gave here, you said that you generally knew the tasks performed by Mr. Zaric and his responsibilities. Since there are certain things that are unclear regarding this, it is unclear to me and to Mr. Zaric, and as a result of that, I would like to inform you of certain things that Mr. Zaric claims are true regarding his employment and will ask you to confirm that for me. The first thing I will ask you to confirm for me is whether Mr. Zaric was the chief of police in Bosanski Samac municipality, or as you called that office, he was secretary of the Secretariat of the Interior in the time period between 13th of May --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the dates. If the counsel could please repeat them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, all of these things that took place up until 1992, and especially those matters that have to do with my suffering, is something that I try to forget, and I try to turn that into my past experience that needs to be forgotten. So I have to apologise if I misstated a year here or there, but I know it for a fact that starting in 1975 or 1976, Mr. Zaric worked in the Secretariat of the Interior, where, according to the then law in force, he was the main person in the secretariat, and I know that he served for two terms, which should be somewhere about eight years.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, since the interpreters didn't manage to interpret the dates that I gave you, let me tell you about this time period. It was from 13th of May, 1975 until the 1st of September, 1979. I'm telling you this so that the times can be properly recorded. So you are telling us that Mr. Zaric served as chief of police for two terms in Bosanski Samac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When I was going over the transcript of your evidence, I saw some things that I would like to clarify with you now. When the Prosecutor asked you about the office of the secretary of the secretariat, he asked you whether that referred to the office in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and you replied yes, based on which somebody could make a wrong conclusion that Mr. Zaric was the secretary of the secretariat of Bosnia and Herzegovina. But in fact what you referred to was the secretariat in Bosanski Samac; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Let me clarify this. The gentleman in question was the secretary of the Secretariat of the Interior in Bosanski Samac, and this secretariat was under the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Based on that, we can conclude that at the time the province of Mr. Zaric's responsibility was the municipality of Bosanski Samac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Then you went on to discuss other things regarding Mr. Zaric, and you said that he was the director of Buducnost company from Samac. Can you confirm for me now that this post, meaning the director of the Buducnost company from Samac, which was within the company called Sipad in Sarajevo, was something that Mr. Zaric performed between 1979 and 1982, when he assumed another office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will ask you not to hold me to the specific years. Whether it was in 1979 or later, I can't tell you. I know that he served for two terms, and then after that he became the director of Sipad, or rather, Buducnost, as it was called in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Naturally, I will not insist on making you quote the specific year. This is something that we need to agree with our colleagues from the Prosecution. But I will ask you a few more things just to clarify this further. So after this office that Mr. Zaric held, when he was the director of Buducnost, after that he was, from the 1st of September, 1982, until 1985, director of Sipad's representative office in Belgrade. Can you confirm that for me, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can confirm to you is this: That Mr. Zaric served for two terms as secretary of the secretariat in Bosanski Samac, after which he went on to work in Buducnost; and after that, I do not remember exactly whether he went to work for Sipad in Belgrade, as a representative of that company there, or whether he perhaps went to the centre of the state security in Doboj, or rather, whether he went to its detachment in Modrica, I mean the state security's detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have an additional question pertaining to this that you have just told us about Mr. Simo Zaric serving two terms as the secretary of the Secretariat of the Interior at the municipal level. Could you please tell us how long is the term of office of the secretary of the Secretariat of the Interior? I mean the municipal secretariat.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at that time, the term of office was four years. Allegedly a person could serve for only two terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We can conclude, then, that Mr. Zaric served for eight years as the secretary of the Secretariat of the Interior in Bosanski Samac, based on what you have just told us; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if he served for two terms, then it's quite clear that two times four is eight. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, it may not be a particularly important point, but it might be sensible to know if they were consecutive terms or whether two separate terms at different times in four years.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I can clarify that with the witness. I have no problem with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you heard the question from the Prosecutor. Were these consecutive terms or two separate terms, which means that from the -- between the first four-year term and the second two-year term, perhaps Mr. Zaric performed some other jobs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the time when he was appointed as the secretary of the secretariat, he held that post in continuity, throughout this period. There was no disruption of his post, term in office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that as of the 1st of September, 1985, Mr. Zaric worked in the State Security Service in the centre of the Security Service in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I don't recall the years, but if in 1975 [as interpreted] he worked in Samac, then he could not have worked in Doboj at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. My question referred to 1985, and that's what is recorded in the transcript. Perhaps you didn't hear me right. We're talking about 1985, not 1975.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I heard you say "1975."

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, at any rate, as of 1985, did Mr. Simo Zaric work for the State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after he left Buducnost, when he was no longer the director in Buducnost, he joined the State Security Service in the Doboj centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question pertaining to the jobs that Mr. Simo Zaric had had between 1986 and the 1st of September, 1991, when Mr. Zaric retired, can you confirm that in that period Mr. Simo Zaric was the head of the Modrica detachment of the State Security Service centre in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he worked in the State Security Service centre in Doboj. He dealt with certain tasks, performed some kind of jobs that I am not aware of. And when he went to Odzak, when he was transferred to Odzak as the detachment head - in other words, it was a forward section, and the headquarters were located in Modrica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would now like to move on to another topic. Could you please go to page 8 of your statement. That would be paragraph 30. Could you please let me know when you've found it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's page 9, in fact, of my copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 30, which begins with the words "on the 17th of April, at around 2.00 a.m." Can you please confirm whether that's the paragraph you're looking at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Regarding this paragraph, I notice that you mention a walkie-talkie here. I would like to ask you a few questions in this regard. Is this a Motorola walkie-talkie?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This would be a standard-issue police Motorola that other members of the police force had; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Samac they had such equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I was not quite clear. I am only interested in the police force in Bosanski Samac. So could you please tell me whether it is true that the members of the reserve and of the active police force had the same type of Motorolas in Samac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: So I can conclude, based on your answer, that Namik Suljic had the exact same Motorola. He was the commander of the reserve police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had one with him that very evening, and I don't know who else had one, but those people who were securing the bridge, the people who were in the town, there were perhaps about four or five such Motorolas, and they were issued to people, and they only functioned on a channel or a frequency where one could get in touch with the duty officer in the station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. These are precisely the questions that I wanted to ask you in this respect. If I understand you correctly, you used the term "single-channel Motorola." That means that one could communicate only on a single channel; you could not communicate over several channels. Do I understand it correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we all worked on one channel. Let me just say that the Motorolas were already obsolete. They were the old-type Motorolas, so that their range was limited. The maximum range was more or less five to six kilometres. They could receive signals in that range. Or, in other words, one could hear things over the Motorola, even if one was further away, but you could not transmit your message to another person, because they were quite weak.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, at any rate, you were able to communicate over this channel exclusively with the station where the HQ was; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On that day - we're talking about the 17th of April, 1992 - you were not on duty; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, the 17th of April, I was supposed to be on duty in the evening. If the need arose, I was supposed to assist Mr. Namik Suljic, and the assistance was more or less in terms of driving the members of the reserve police force to wherever they had to go or to take them from the local communes to the MUP building, and from there to the bridge and to other facilities that were secured at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, you answered me regarding the 17th of April. Were you on duty on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We have the information that when a duty police officer who is on duty finishes his service, that he is supposed to return his Motorola to the station after the end of his shift.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not exactly how it is. If you want me to tell you, the Motorolas would just be handed over to the next person coming on. He would simply change the battery.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was more or less my next question, because we have the information that the Motorolas could not be operated indefinitely, that they had to be recharged. But I assume that now that you've explained this to us, that would be sufficient, more or less. Now I would like to go on to paragraph 31 of your statement. Could you please have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the transcript, I am interested in the part where you discuss Mr. Slavko Glamocak, a member of the 4th Detachment, as you say, and you indicated you learned later that he had gone to the telephone, to the post office, and disconnected the lines. Can you please tell me -- you said you learned that later. Can you please tell me: Who did you learn it from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would like to describe this case at some length, and how I obtained this information about Mr. Glamocak being a member of the 4th Detachment, and I know for a fact, and I am convinced, that he had gone to the post office and disconnected the phone lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the fact that Mr. Glamocak was a member of the 4th Detachment is not in dispute, but see here: If you answer in detail to every question that I ask you, I'm afraid that my questioning will take much longer than the time that the Prosecution took. I'm asking you questions that you will be able to answer in a very simple manner, and I assure you that the Prosecution, if they think that they need to obtain any clarification from you, they will be able to ask you questions, all those questions that they deem to be necessary, in the course of the re-direct. Right now I need the name of the person who told you that Slavko Glamocak had disconnected the phone lines. That's the only thing I'm interested in, the name of that person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you first of all that I have to clarify some things. I came here to tell the truth, and let me answer the question now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Witness A, just answer the questions put to you by counsel. We have other witnesses yet to come, and as counsel explained to you, the Prosecution will still have time to clarify anything. So just answer the questions as they come. Do not explain anything, unless counsel asks you to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Witness A, could you please tell me the name of the person who told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted] His name is Sakib Sahacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you just tell me when did you obtain this information? When did you hear that from [redacted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember when it was that we discussed this, but let me tell you that it was after I was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [redacted], he did not work in the PTT, I mean Mr. Sakib Sahacic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look very quickly at paragraph 34. You have it in front of you. [redacted] Mihajlo Topolovac, Slavko Glamocak, Mladen Dordjic, as it says here. I believe his name is actually Djordic, Vaso Antic, and Slavko Nikolic are discussed here. All those [redacted] are of Serb ethnic origin, from what I can gather from their names, the ones that I just mentioned; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And all those [redacted] that I mentioned were in their homes on that evening, at the night between the 16th and the 17th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And all those Serb [redacted] that I mentioned were members of the 4th Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about Slavko Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But you are sure about the others; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And it was no secret that they were members of the 4th Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would now like to move on to paragraph 41.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to ask for a break, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I don't know if he's doing well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. We shall take our break, and the legal officer will let us know when it will be convenient to continue with the proceedings. The Court will rise. --- Break taken at 3.07 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: One very brief matter. Before we adjourn this afternoon briefly before the next witness and the next episode of evidence this afternoon, could I just have a minute to address you regarding witnesses and the further progress this week? Thank you. Not now, but at the end -- just prior to this -- or just upon the break of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before we go on the break? MR. DI FAZIO: That's right, yes, so that I can just raise some housekeeping matters for the rest of the week. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll continue until 20 minutes before 4.00, because the video conference link has to be arranged, and then we have to start at 4.00 sharp in order to have as much time as possible. So you can proceed, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, we have a little more time in which we should try to do as much as possible. I asked you to have a look at paragraph 41 of your statement, which starts with the words "then they shoved me into the car." In this respect, I would like to ask you a question: Who shoved you into Josip Orsolic's car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was shoved into the car by Nebojsa Stankovic, nicknamed Cera, and Slobodan Miljkovic, nicknamed Lugar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. After that you were taken in that car to the police station. Now, I would like to know: When you arrived at the police station, were the Serb police officers there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The Serb police officers, did they wear berets on their heads, dark-blue berets, greyish blue, as part of their uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And all this happened in the duty police officer's room, the events that you described in paragraph 41; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, since you worked for many years as a police officer in the Samac police station, I think that you are the witness who could provide us with certain pieces of information which primarily have to do with the layout of the rooms in the Bosanski Samac police station, and that's why I would like us to look at some photographs, and then if you could assist me about where certain offices or rooms are located.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At this moment I would like to have some assistance from the usher. I would like to show to the witness -- evidence is P14. This is a set of photographs. And I need photograph F53. And if I could just first take a look at that photograph and then to be shown to the witness. Your Honours, I'm not certain if this is the photograph that was marked with a certain number. Maybe I should take a look again, just not to make any mistakes. Oh, yes. This is a set of photographs with the indicator what is on it, and we already made a ruling in this respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We shall use P14A. That's the one without any labels on the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the usher please get the photograph from the witness. He will be given the -- yes. Can we get the photograph from the witness. He should be shown the photograph from P14A. There's another bundle of photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And for the benefit of our clients and the Bench also, maybe it would be best to place it on the ELMO so everyone can see what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you've had a look at this photograph. Could you please tell me: Which building is depicted on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the MUP building in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. On the basis of what we see on this photograph, can we agree that it consists of the ground floor and another storey, the first floor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please show me on this photograph where the duty police officer's room or office is located. Please use the pointer that you have, and you can point to that room on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, let me tell you that this is the photograph taken from the yard. So this is the internal part of the building, facing the yard. The first window to the left --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't want to interrupt you. I'm sorry. But when you're talking about a window or something, could you please point at it to your right on the ELMO, because we cannot see you if you're pointing on your screen.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the way to do it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the window of the duty officer's room, and this is also the window of the duty officer's room. So his room had two windows: One, two. And it looked out onto the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: May the record reflect that the witness has shown two windows on the ground floor, left from the entrance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The next two windows going to the left, next to the duty officer's room, on which rooms were these two windows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really remember that well. I think that the third window here may have been the window on the office next door, or perhaps this may also have been the window of the duty officer's room, but very close to the wall. I really don't remember, but I'm absolutely sure that the first two windows belonged to the duty officer's office, and this third window here may have been the window on an office adjacent to the duty officer's office, but they were divided by a wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now I would also ask again: I don't think I need this photograph any more, but I would like photograph F43 to be shown to the witness. It's P14A, F43.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Has the registry got P14A?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I couldn't find it in my trolley.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is not a map, Your Honours. Actually, this is -- P14A is a set of photographs, so I was just asking for photograph 43. MR. DI FAZIO: It must be there. It's part of the exhibit that we've already extracted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It appears that maybe P14A is not available. Is it available?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Can I use P14 instead?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, maybe we could place some piece of paper or something so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. What I see from those which have labels, they simply name the building; they don't name the actual offices. So it really doesn't matter if he uses P14.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I will not complain. I mean, there was not any dispute that this is a photograph of the building of the police station, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So he can use the same photograph, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can we agree that this is the same building, but this photograph was taken from the street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, if we look at the building from this side, from the street, can you please show where the offices that were used by Dragan Lukac at that time, who was the acting secretary, and where, according to your testimony, Lugar took you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the entrance, and the office had to be here, because it also had the balcony. So this is the room. I'm not sure about this window, whether it was a window in this room or not, but I'm absolutely sure about this window here because one could go out onto the balcony from that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may the record reflect that the witness indicated the space with the balcony on the upper-right corner of the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You mean of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of this building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to show me where the police commander's office was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS A [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this may have been the one, here, because I only can tell you the following: This was the office where the acting secretary was, Lukac; then there was another room next to it; and another room next to it. So that would be the third room from this one. So I'm not quite sure which window it was. I believe that it may have been -- well, to tell you the truth, this building reminds me of some really nasty events, so I really have to apologise. I'm not sure whether this is the window or the other one. I only know the sequence of the offices. I believe that it may be this one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe you when you say that this reminds you of some really nasty events, but we really have to clear this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... that the witness indicated the third window on the upper floor of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counting from where?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Counting from the right, right side of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And Your Honours, is it time for us to take a break? Because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I've been reminded that he wasn't sure -- the witness wasn't sure, if you remember. He was pointing at the third or the fourth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was understood from his answers, but he indicated third or fourth. And I will not insist on that any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. I think we have to take a break, and the witness, we'll continue with him tomorrow, in the afternoon, since we have to take on the videolink, which is fixed. And can he be led out of the courtroom. We'll continue with your evidence tomorrow at 1415. Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. It's just a question of how to plan for the rest of the week, and I'd seek some guidance from the Chamber. We have Witness A, who will be taking up the earlier part of the afternoons, and then the second part, of course, with the videolink. Now, apparently Defence counsel have indicated they won't be too long with Witness A, but we've still got some way to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And even with -- and with the videolink, I would think that that's going to take a substantial part of the remainder of the week, with evidence in chief and then cross-examination, and then any re-examination that may occur. We've got two witnesses, two forthcoming witnesses, the husband-and-wife team. I think the Chamber is aware of them. They're in The Hague at the moment. They've finished any proofing matters and so on. And if we keep them here, they're going to be here, in effect, for the rest of the week on the off chance that they may give some evidence towards the end of the week. Now, we'll do that if the Chamber wishes, but the way I see things going is that this witness and the videolink is going to take up a substantial part of the remainder of the week, and then Friday, I believe, is -- we're not sitting, unless I'm greatly mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. There's court maintenance. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. So can I have your approval to speak to Victims and Witnesses Unit and send them back and bring them back at a later time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe it would be a good idea to have one witness waiting. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because, you see, the problem with the videolink is it can only start at 4.00 p.m. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It can't start earlier than that. MR. DI FAZIO: I appreciate that. I understand that. I'm just thinking, Your Honours, if you look at it this way, he's just started with one Defence counsel, and I'm told estimates are ranging around over an hour each. So three of them, then re-examination, and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will let you know after the break. MR. DI FAZIO: Okay. If -- thank you. I'd be grateful to you if you could perhaps have an opportunity to confer and then give us some direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We will take a break now until 4.00 p.m. --- Break taken at 3.42 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. The witness can sit down. Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May I begin?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would you please identify yourself to the Court.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Subasic, could you tell us how old you are?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me. We have no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I'm 33 years old.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Now we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where were you born, sir?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I was born in Odzak, on the 4th of November, 1969.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when did you move to Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Sometime in 1971.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So when you were about 2 years old. And up to April of 1992, did you spend the rest of your life in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am married.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I have two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Of what ethnic group do you come from?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I'm a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And your wife, of what ethnic group is she?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: My wife is Catholic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So she would be a Croatian; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, in April of 1992, where were you living, sir?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: In Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you living in a home or an apartment, a house or an apartment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: In an apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And who was living with you at the time?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: My mother, my wife, and daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And sir, could you tell us what street, if you recall, the apartment was on?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Edvarda Kardelja Street, apartment building 64.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did some relatives of yours also have homes within Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did they have two homes within a complex, or two homes on the same piece of property?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Not within the same complex. A few blocks apart. A few blocks further on from the apartment. They had two houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. It was not in the same complex where you lived, but were the two houses that your family members had, were they on the same piece of property, on the same piece of land, the two houses together, not the two houses and your apartment.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were those members of your mother's family?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how long had your mother's family lived in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Several generations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you attend school in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did; the elementary and the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you study a specific vocation in the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, a trade. I became a welder.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And upon graduation, did you go to work somewhere?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I went to work in a company called Mebos.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where is that located, sir?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: On the outskirts of Samac, Edvarda Kardelja Street as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you serve in the military on a full-time basis in the 1980s?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where were you sent?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: To Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what sort of unit did you work in or were you assigned to?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Anti-aircraft unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when did you complete that military service, Mr. Subasic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I think it was in 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, after completing your military service, did you become part of the TO, or did you join the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you own or possess a firearm while you lived in Bosanski Samac, after your military years?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you have a hunting rifle?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you ever become a member of the new TO, which was commanded by Alija Fitozovic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you ever join any type of military unit prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, were you a member of any political party?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was your wife a member of any political party?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you some questions about the defendants in this case. Having lived practically your whole life in Bosanski Samac --

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we seem to be having some trouble with the video. Should I hold?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've been told by the AV to keep going. We're okay now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry. We had some technical difficulties there for a minute with the picture. So having lived your whole life in Bosanski Samac, I'm going to ask you about a few people. Do you know a man by the name of Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Well, I know him by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How long have you known him by sight?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Some 20 years or more.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how did you come to know him by sight?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: The son of his wife went to the elementary school with me; Denis Topcagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you good friends with Denis Topcagic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you ever go to his home to socialise when you were children?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when you went to his home, did you ever see Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know a man by the name of Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: A man who uses the nickname of Brko, or "the moustache"?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How do you know Miroslav Tadic, or Brko?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: He had a shop in Samac, and I frequently went there to shop.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that the witness might have said that he knew Miroslav Tadic. It was unclear. So perhaps that question could be repeated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, we didn't hear your first answer. The question was: Do you -- or did you know a man by the name of Miroslav Tadic, nicknamed Brko?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And in addition to a store or some sort of grocery store, did he have another business?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Afterwards, he had a cafe called AS.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And had you ever visited the Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: A few times perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Finally, did you know a man by the name of Blagoje Simic, Dr. Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Superficially, by sight only.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him prior to April 17th, 1992, in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What about during the war? Did you ever see him?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Once, on one occasion, when I was imprisoned in the TO building. I don't remember when exactly it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where was he when you were imprisoned in the TO building? Where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: In the yard of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are you referring to the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not certain at this point, should I -- should we try and have him attempt to identify the defendants here or should we move on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Well, if it's possible, yes, because he can see the courtroom. Yes, it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's attempt that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If you could look around the courtroom, could you tell us if you can see Simo Zaric, having known him for many years, or known him by sight for many years?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you tell us how -- could you tell us how they're dressed? Let's start off with Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: He has a black jacket, red tie, as far as I can see from here, and a white shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What about Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: A white shirt, black jacket, dark tie. I can't tell which colour it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us something about on his face, or the colour of his hair, or if there's anything on his face that's significant to you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see from here, he has grey hair, grey moustache.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what about Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I think that he's sitting between the two of them. He has a beard, a white shirt. I can't tell which colour is his tie. And he's somewhat bald.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect that all three defendants have been identified by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you indicated you were a welder. In November of 1991, could you tell us where you were working?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you -- you were a welder at the time. Did you receive a promotion or did they change your position in 1991?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we didn't receive any translation on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We didn't get any translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear us now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. I'll ask the question again. In November of 1991, did you receive a promotion, or did you receive a new position at the Mebos plant in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I worked on the security that was stepped up in the Mebos company.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you were no longer working as a welder there?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let's continue on into 1992. Between January and April, mid-April of 1992, did you attend any political meetings or rallies?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Only once. I think it was March or February. After an accident that happened in the Cafe Valentino, where two persons got killed, there was a citizens' rally, and I attended it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you recall who spoke or what was said at that rally?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you attend any other rallies or any political meetings during that same period in 1992?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: On one occasion, when we were required to come to an area in front of the Buducnost factory, but that was at the time when the war had already broken out in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. So prior to the war, you didn't attend any political meetings or rallies other than the citizens' meeting after the two people were killed and the young lady was injured at the Valentino Cafe; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In 1992, were you involved in any citizen patrols or civil defence?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you involved in the setting up or manning of any of the barricades?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, in addition to the job that you had at the Mebos, were you working at night? Did you have a side job, sir?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I did work the night shift at the Mebos factory, and sometimes I would fix things, appliances, for people, for instance, the water heaters and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So basically, during that period you were involved in just raising your family?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, were you aware of a unit in Bosanski Samac known as the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you know any of the members of that unit?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how did you know these people?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Well, quite a few of them were my friends. Samac is a small town, and most people knew everybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were any of the defendants members of the 4th Detachment, sir?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I believe they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Which defendants were members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I know for sure that Simo Zaric and Miroslav Tadic were members, and I don't know about Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Was there any special cafe or location where members of the 4th Detachment would meet and associate?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Mostly in Miroslav Tadic's cafe, which was called AS.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the role of the 4th Detachment? What was it supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know for sure what its role was. I heard from those people that it was supposed to defend Samac, but I don't know against whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did it protect all the citizens of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Which citizens, or citizens from which ethnic group were not protected by the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Well, one could tell that from the fact who was imprisoned in Bosanski Samac. That was mostly Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on, sir. Let's move on to the night that the war began, the early-morning hours of April 17th, approximately 1.00, 2.00 a.m., could you tell us where you were?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I was in my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you hear anything at that time?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Well, I heard shooting from the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you go out during those early-morning hours, around 1.00, 2.00, 3.00, or 4.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No, but I got out around 6.00 or 6.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Later that morning - 6.00, 6.30, 7.00 - where did you go when you went out?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I went to the house of my mother-in-law, to see what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where did she live?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: The old name was Pere Bosica Street, number 92.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we have some problems with the transcript. What we heard from this witness, he said, "my old mother," and here we have a translation "mother-in-law." So basically this could maybe in further ... Well, I don't know. Some problems, maybe identifying what place, what street or something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. Deal with that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The person whose home you went to, was that your grandmother?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And she lived on Pere Bosica Street?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes. The house number was 92.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you go there by vehicle or did you walk to the house?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I went there on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you carrying a weapon of any kind when you went there?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you got there, what did you observe?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: My neighbours were out in the street. We were not aware of what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you stay at your grandmother's home very long?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. Perhaps half an hour or 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where did you go after you left your grandmother's home?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I went back to my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as you walked back to your apartment, did you observe anything?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I observed quite a few things. I had to pass by the AS Cafe, and I saw quite a few armed people in the cafe, and I knew quite a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: What else did you see?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In addition to seeing the armed persons at the cafe AS, the armed soldiers, did you see anything else on the way home?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you know a man by the name of Esad Dagovic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. He is a very good friend of mine. We know each other from childhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you see Esad Dagovic that morning as you walked home?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where did you see him?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: In the Pere Bosica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did he live on that street?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, he lived on that street.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And where was he in relation to his home?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Perhaps 20 or 30 metres from his home.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was he carrying a rifle or automatic weapon of any kind when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't see anything, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you eventually returned home. Did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, later that day, on April 17th, either late morning or in the afternoon, did something happen?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes. They came to my apartment. My apartment was searched. It was in the late afternoon of the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's take it one step at a time. When you say "they," are you referring to soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When did you first see the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: That morning when I went out, that was the first time that I saw the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were at home, did you see the soldiers from your window?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did see them from the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, when you saw the soldiers from the window, were any of the defendants with them?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And what were they doing at the time? Were they walking? Were they in a vehicle? Were they sitting on the ground? What were they doing, the two defendants?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: They were in a vehicle, going from apartment to apartment, from one entrance to another, searching the apartments, looking for weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How many soldiers were with the defendants Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I think between 10 and 15 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How were Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric dressed when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: They wore military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, could you hear from your window Miroslav Tadic or Simo Zaric saying anything?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I heard them issue orders about which apartments were to be entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did they say anything in relation to the guns?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Could you please elaborate, explain your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry. Did they say anything in relation to pointing of a gun or pointing of one's guns?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Well, the rifles were pointed at the apartments where they went to search.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did the soldiers, Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric eventually stop at your apartment building?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did they enter the apartment building?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court where they went after they entered the apartment building, where they went and what they did?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: First they searched the apartment belonging to the person by the name of Dedic. I don't know his full name. I think that Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric knew him quite well. So they searched his apartment. They broke down the door, searched the apartment, and then they went on searching other apartments.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's take this slowly. Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric get out of the vehicle and enter your apartment building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How many soldiers entered the apartment building with those two defendants?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. Some five or six, but could be more as well. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, this person whose home was searched, whose apartment was searched, was that on the first floor?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And is that a person by the name of Dedo Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And while the soldiers were searching Dedo Halilovic's apartment, did Simo Zaric or Miroslav Tadic make any statements about Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes. They said he was a terrorist, that he was the head of the SDA party, that he had a sniper, and later on they checked whether there were any openings on the top of the building, looking for the openings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did they make any remarks indicating that Mr. Halilovic was involved in the resistance, or what they referred to as the resistance?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric state that Mr. Halilovic was involved with what they referred to as the resistance?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you know this Mr. Halilovic, sir?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was he a soldier?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No, he was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you find those statements odd?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. There was simply no resistance in Samac whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And was this Mr. Halilovic any type of warrior or special forces officer or terrorist?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No, he was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did these soldiers come to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did anyone speak with you when they came to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes. Miroslav Tadic, Simo Zaric, and other soldiers. I don't remember their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did they ask you about weapons?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: They asked me whether I had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how did you answer?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: That I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did they enter your apartment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did, and they searched it superficially. They didn't break anything or make any damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric enter your apartment with the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How long were the soldiers and the defendants in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Perhaps some 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, where did they go after they left your apartment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I think they went searching the other apartments, and then they left the building, but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were the apartments of persons of a certain ethnic group or groups searched?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I think that it was only Muslim and Catholic apartments that were searched.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did they search the roof?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Before the soldiers left and before the two defendants left, did they say anything to you in relation to Dedo Halilovic or anything else?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: They said that we should watch out for the opening on the roof, and should we hear or see Dedo, to let them know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How long had they been in the apartment building?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. Perhaps 40 or 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on to the next week, from April 18th through 24th. Do you recall what you did during those seven days?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: I went back to my company, Mebos. I worked there as a receptionist.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was the plant functioning?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: The company was not functioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did employees from all the ethnic groups come to work?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Well, not really. Maybe just a couple of employees reported, but that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How many hours did you work a day during that week?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Some days I worked up to 20 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, were you serving also or working also in a capacity of security while you were there?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you armed?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Yes. I had a pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Where did you get the pistol?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: It was owned by the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And did you use that pistol or carry it with you when you worked security prior to April 17th?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, what was happening at the Mebos plant during that week while you were working as a security officer, while you worked your regular job as a security officer?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: There was much looting going on. They came with tractors and trailers and they would take out the goods manufactured in Mebos.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Who was looting the goods at the Mebos plant?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters could not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you the question again. Apparently the interpreters could not hear your answer. Who was looting the property from the Mebos plant?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: Local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: How were they taking the property back or away with them?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: In tractors, small trucks called Tamic, in trailers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you stop the looters from taking these goods?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
utterances.text: All of them were armed. They had automatic rifles and military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did any of these people threaten you or bother you while you were at the Mebos plant?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC
